VERDICT: flag

RATIONALE: The MIN is bounded above by E/P, so high values are substantially driven by cheapness (a positive predictor), contradicting the stated negative expected sign, and the "cheap-on-reported-earnings-but-accrual-funded" trap channel was already tested as the Reported Clean Earnings Rank Gap.

---CRITIQUE Cash Surplus Earnings Bottleneck---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: MIN(E/P, −accruals/P) is a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived One Sided Accrual Capped Earnings Yield (MIN(ib, ib−accruals)/P), differing only in whether the earnings level is retained in the second leg, so it is unlikely to deliver substantively new evidence.

---CRITIQUE Cash Surplus Book Bottleneck---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 1
RATIONALE: Book-to-price is typically an order of magnitude larger than accruals-to-price, so the MIN will almost always select the accrual leg and the signal degenerates into a plain price-scaled Sloan accrual measure rather than the intended value×accrual interaction.

---CRITIQUE Underdepreciation Expense Trap---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is the isolated trap leg of the already-evaluated Underdepreciation Discounted Book Yield with no value interaction, is close to the known Lev–Thiagarajan/Abarbanell–Bushee depreciation-change fundamental signal, and the one-sided MAX leaves a large mass of exact zeros that will make one portfolio leg unstable.

---CRITIQUE Conservative Depreciation Earnings Yield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Adding back only the firm-relative abnormal excess depreciation to earnings is a coherent, sign-consistent value×conservative-accounting construct that is a genuine complement (not a mirror) to the archived underdepreciation-discount signal and uses a distinct accrual channel from the working-capital family that dominates the archive.

---CRITIQUE EBITDA Working Capital Trap Bottleneck---
